situation: Checkout latency spiked and enterprise customers were failing mid-task; an engineer wanted to root-cause live before rolling back.
decision: Capture evidence, roll back the morning's config change immediately, and analyse the cause in a review the next day.

moves.name: ask what changed recently
moves.step: Before investigating symptoms, list what changed in the last hour and suspect it first.
moves.cue: a sudden regression shortly after a deploy
moves.evidence: before anyone opens a profiler: what changed this morning?

moves.name: stabilise first, diagnose second
moves.step: Stop the customer harm with a cheap mitigation before spending time on root cause.
moves.cue: customers failing while engineers want to investigate

moves.name: identify who carries the cost
moves.step: Name who bears the cost of each option, especially of delay.
moves.cue: a proposal to keep the fault live while investigating
moves.evidence: they are the ones carrying the cost of our investigation, not us

moves.name: choose the reversible action first
moves.step: Prefer the action you can undo in minutes over the one you cannot.
moves.cue: a candidate fix that is a small config rollback
moves.evidence: The rollback is a two-minute change we can undo, so it costs us almost nothing to try it first.

moves.name: capture evidence before the rollback
moves.step: Snapshot dumps, metrics and diffs before mitigating so diagnosis can happen later.
moves.cue: fear of losing the state needed for root cause
moves.evidence: grab a heap dump and the limiter metrics ... that is your evidence and it will still be there this afternoon

moves.name: commit to next update time
moves.step: Tell affected customers when they will next hear from you, regardless of progress.
moves.cue: customers calling support during an incident
moves.evidence: they will hear from us again at 09:40 whether or not it is fixed

considerations.evidence: it will still be there this afternoon
